targets.keyword: ballet second position in frozen narrow flat-foot variant

components.criterion: two owned feet apart slightly beyond hip width on same floor plane
both toes turn outward in opposite directions
both soles and heels are grounded

targets.evidence: The turned-out feet are flat and separate, but the stance is conspicuously broad compared with the frozen slightly-wider-than-hips spacing. Generic second-position resemblance does not satisfy that narrower qualifier.

components.criterion: each knee tracks the direction of its own toes
pelvis remains between feet under upright torso

targets.evidence: The knees are deeply flexed and the pelvis is lowered far into a broad squat-like plie. This is not the frozen shallow bend. No force or exact joint angle is inferred.

components.criterion: soft elbows make one rounded oval
hands above head with a fingertip air gap

targets.evidence: Both connected arms form a clear overhead oval; elbows curve, hands remain separate above the head, and shoulders do not shrug toward the ears.

body_ownership.reason: Both connected arm and leg chains belong to the same subject.

joint_chain_and_reach.reason: Shoulder/elbow/wrist and hip/knee/ankle paths are legible and plausible.

support_and_balance.reason: Both flat feet support the centered pelvis beneath the upright torso.

contact_and_space.reason: Both slipper heels and forefeet visibly meet the dry platform; hands remain separate.

visibility_and_projection.reason: The whole overhead oval, both knees, toes and floor contacts are visible.

scene_reason: Conservatory, wardrobe, musical props and light match, but the frozen stance width and shallow knee bend do not.
reference_use: Visible dark bob, wispy bangs and facial appearance guidance; no identity or biometric judgment.
